field_body_right_.value:
Visit The Great Port gallery to discover how Liverpool transformed from a small tidal inlet into one of the world’s greatest and well-known port.

Lighting

There are low light levels within this gallery.  

  • Spotlights are used to help view the collections
  • Some information panels are backlit, which can be bright

Please take care and avoid areas with bright backlighting and spotlights if you are sensitive to light.  If you have tinted glasses it would be useful to bring them. 

Format

Many videos in The Great Port gallery have options for British Sign Language interpretation and closed captions. They include Induction Loops.

Interactives

The Great Port gallery includes some tactile displays and a sensory smell display. If you want to ensure that these interactives are available before your visit please get in touch.

field_body_right_.value:
This part of the museum explores the experience of living in the city.

Access route and flooring

The court housing reconstruction gives visitors a chance to step back in time and view what houses used to be like in Liverpool. Please take care when entering this part of the gallery due to the uneven flooring and narrow access routes.

Lighting

Natural lighting is used throughout most of this gallery, except for the initial entrance to the gallery and the court housing reconstruction.

Format

Throughout this gallery you will find audio-visual information including closed captions, British Sign Language interpretation and induction loops.

Information in this gallery is mainly white text on a red background, with limited use of Braille.

Interactives

Within this gallery there are a variety of interactives located within the court housing reconstruction.

Noise pollution

The People’s Republic is a large gallery with high levels of noise pollution, particularly around the video displays. You may benefit from having headphones or ear buds if you are sensitive to noise.

Viewpoint

Behind the cathedral display you will see the spectacular views of Liverpool’s Liver Birds. This is a great spot to take a break, however there is limited seating within this area.

Trigger warning

If you follow to the left once having entered the gallery you will come across an audio-visual of war footage. Visitors can hear gun fire, high pitch whistles and shouting. These sounds can be heard within other areas of the gallery. There are scenes of deceased soldiers. If you think someone within your visiting group may be affected by this, please use the access route to right of the gallery entrance.
